Like, my husband and I were supposed to sit down and figure out the budget for redoing the guest room—which really needs it, the paint is peeling and it's this awful yellow color from the nineties. We were watching this home renovation show the other day, the one with the twins? I can never remember their names, but they always use open shelving in the kitchens, which I think is just a massive dust trap. I don't know who has the time to wash all their plates before they even use them, you know? I definitely don't. 

But anyway... yeah, whenever I have to actually sit at the table and look at the paperwork for things like that, I just... I can't get comfortable. I just feel totally restless.

turns.doctor_question: Do you often act out or argue with people when they try to direct or correct you?

I don't know why she insists on making it from scratch when the bakery down the street makes a perfectly good one. And she uses this weird crust recipe that tastes like cardboard. I actually saw her dog spit a piece out once. The dog's name is Barnaby, he's a pug, and he breathes so loud it sounds like a coffee maker. turns.doctor_question: Do you often interrupt people or blurt out answers before they’ve finished speaking?

It’s like the response just comes out of my mouth before I’ve even made myself wait. 

I do it to my husband constantly. Just yesterday he was talking to our neighbor, Greg, about his lawnmower. Greg has this massive riding mower, which makes zero sense because his yard is tiny. It’s barely a patch of grass, honestly. He spends more time backing the thing out of his shed than he does actually cutting the grass. And he always wears these huge, bright orange noise-canceling headphones when he does it, like he’s directing airplanes on a runway or something. I don't know where he even bought them, probably that hardware store one town over that always has those weird clearance bins at the front. I bought a set of miniature screwdrivers from one of those bins once, thinking they'd be good for fixing my sunglasses, but they all snapped the very first time I tried to use them. Cheap metal, I guess. 

But, um... yeah, my husband was trying to explain something to Greg, and I just kept blurting out the end of his sentences. I just can't seem to hold the words in.

And my husband dropped his phone down into the crack between the seats right before the previews started. She always wore these matching pastel pantsuits, too, usually mint green or baby blue. She had this massive collection of porcelain frogs on her desk. It was so weird. I accidentally knocked one over once when I was handing in a spelling test, and the little porcelain banjo it was holding snapped right off. She's thinking about getting a puppy, a golden retriever, and wanted to know if I thought that was a good idea since her youngest just started kindergarten. 

But, um... wait, what were we talking about? Oh, right, when I was a kid. Yeah, the messy desk, the permission slips, the talking out of turn... that was all happening way back in elementary school.
